# Tournament roster corpus

357 real Age of Sigmar tournament lists from 2025–2026, captured verbatim from public event
coverage. Every list is what a player actually pasted into a tournament submission.

Harness: `src/tests/aos4/tournamentCorpus.test.ts`
Provenance: `manifest.json` — one entry per list, with its source article, event, exporter,
app/data version, byte length and SHA-256.

## Why this corpus exists

The other import corpora are ours. `official-app/` and `sigdex/` are hand-authored captures, one
per shape or per army; the New Recruit corpus is generated to sweep name resolution. All of them
test the exports **we** know how to make.

This one tests the exports **players** send. That turns out to be a different problem:

- roster names left blank, so the export opens on a bare `2000/2000 pts`
- roster names with newlines in them, pushing the points total onto its own line
- names run straight into the total with no space — `…John Cena!!2000/2000 pts`
- footers from 60+ app versions, spread across two `General's Handbook` seasons
- armies that were legal on the day and are not now

The first three were live parser bugs when this corpus was captured; they misread the roster name
as the faction, and they affected 11% of real lists. See "What this corpus found" below.

## Layout

```
tournament/
  manifest.json
  lists/<exporter>/<faction-slug>-<nnn>-<event-slug>/list.txt
```

`<exporter>` is `official-app`, `sigdex` or `listbot`. Faction slugs match the New Recruit and
official-app corpora (`sce`, `syl`, `cos`, …), numbered per faction across the whole corpus.

## Coverage

| | |
| --- | --- |
| lists | 357 — 338 official app, 15 Sigdex, 4 Listbot |
| armies | all 27, from Stormcast Eternals (27 lists) to Bonesplitterz (1) |
| events | 189 distinct tournaments |
| span | 2025 Q1 – 2026 Q3, roughly even by quarter |
| app versions | 60+, from `1.7.0` to `1.35.1 (1)` |
| handbooks | 2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27 |

## Capture method

Lists were harvested from the *Competitive Innovations in the Mortal Realms* archive, which inlines
each list verbatim in the article HTML:

- `https://www.goonhammer.com/category/aos-competitive-innovations/`

WordPress interleaves `<p>`/`</p>` scaffolding at the line breaks, but the underlying paste uses
CRLF and the mangling only ever inserts tags around the CR. **Every CR in the markup is a real line
break**; the `<p>`, `</p>` and LF characters are scaffolding. Stripping the tags and normalising
CRLF/CR to LF therefore round-trips the paste exactly — which is what makes these captures byte-
pinned rather than merely approximate.

A capture was kept only if the repository's own `detectAos4TextSource` recognised its footer, so
every list here carries an intact `Created with Warhammer Age of Sigmar: The App` /
`Created with Sigdex: sigdex.io` / `Generated by Listbot 4.0` marker. Footer-stripped pastes are
common in the wild and are correctly rejected; none are kept here.

Player names are deliberately not recorded. The event, date and source article are provenance
enough to re-verify any capture, and the parser does not care who wrote the list.

## Do not hand-edit

`manifest.json` records each file's SHA-256, and the harness checks it. The separators, blank
lines, stray whitespace and trailing footers are all load-bearing signals the parsers key off —
tidying one destroys the only reason the file is worth keeping. Re-capture instead.

## What the harness checks

There are no per-list goldens. A golden records whatever the parser does today; 357 of them would
be 357 files nobody reads. Every assertion here holds independently of any recorded output:

- the bytes match the manifest checksum
- the roster decodes with **no diagnostics**, and its source matches the recorded exporter
- `declaredFaction` is a name the generated catalog actually carries as a `faction`
- no selection label is scaffolding, empty, or still carrying a points suffix, and every one
  traces back to a non-empty line of the source
- decoding is deterministic and CRLF-insensitive
- resolution against the accepted catalog produces **no error diagnostics**

Unresolved labels are collected into a printed histogram rather than asserted — a label the corpus
lacks is a data gap, and failing the build for one would make this corpus impossible to keep. 201
of the 357 resolve completely; across the corpus 92% of selections resolve.

## What this corpus found

Three defects, all in the header readers, all fixed alongside the capture:

1. **`officialApp.ts`** — the header reader required `<name> 2000/2000 pts` on one line. When the
   total stood alone, or ran into the name without a space, or the name wrapped across lines, the
   first line of the roster name became `declaredFaction`. 23 lists.
2. **`sigdex.ts`** — the same shape, one parser over: the header was read positionally from line
   two rather than from below the points total. 7 lists.
3. **`listbot.ts`** — a bracketed enhancement carrying its cost (`[Bloodshadow Rites (20pts)]`)
   kept the suffix on the label and silently failed to resolve. 1 list.

The fix in all three cases is the same idea: **the header begins after the points total.**

## Known exclusions

31 of the 388 candidate lists are not in the corpus, recorded under `excluded` in the manifest:

- **18** declare `Orruk Warclans` as the faction rather than Ironjawz or Kruleboyz. That is a
  superseded naming the app still emitted through the 2025-26 handbook; the catalog carries no
  such faction and is not going to. Excluded deliberately and permanently — do not read these as
  a catalog gap to close, and do not re-add them when re-capturing.
- **13** carry freeform player prose *between* the points total and the faction row. The header
  cannot be located without consulting the catalog, and importers resolve against the catalog —
  they do not consult it to parse.

## Adding to the corpus

Community-donated captures are welcome under the same layout. Add
`lists/<exporter>/<faction-slug>-<nnn>-<event-slug>/list.txt`, then add its manifest entry with the
correct byte length and SHA-256. The harness will tell you if the two disagree.
